findings.checklist_item: Reconcile the ':prev rollback lifeline' language with the MCP image scheme: state the actual MCP rollback tag to retain (e.g. the LIVE backend's `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` and the immediately-previous SHA), since `$MCP_IMAGE:prev` is never created (only `$BOT_IMAGE:prev` exists).
evidence: autodeploy.sh:676,:679,:689 create/restore `$BOT_IMAGE:prev` — all references to `:prev` in the code are on $BOT_IMAGE (review-bot), not MCP
autodeploy.sh:763 tags the MCP release as `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` (SHA); no `$MCP_IMAGE:prev` is ever created
The comment quoted by the plan (autodeploy.sh:272 ':prev is the rollback lifeline') documents prune_docker_caches, which runs in the review-bot context; it does not describe an MCP :prev tag
findings.finding: The plan directs keeping ':prev' as the MCP rollback lifeline, but ':prev' is only ever created for the review-bot image ($BOT_IMAGE), never for the MCP image; the MCP blue-green path uses immutable SHA-tagged releases ($MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET) with no ':prev' tag.
findings.location: Scope #1 and Acceptance Criteria lines 1-2 ('Keep the LIVE image and `:prev` as the rollback lifeline')
scenarios: Author writes the retire-path tag-removal keyed on preserving `$MCP_IMAGE:prev`, but no such tag exists, so the intended safeguard is a no-op / the AC test can't assert a surviving `:prev` MCP tag

findings.checklist_item: Specify how the retire path maps a reaped container (12-char truncated SHA in its name) to its full-SHA `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` image tag (e.g. via `docker inspect` of the container's image ID), since the truncated container name does not directly yield the full-SHA image tag.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:783 `mcp_newname="${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}"` — container name uses truncated (12-char) SHA
autodeploy.sh:763 `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` — image tag uses the FULL SHA
mcp_retire_sweep at :448-462 iterates container names ($n) only; it has the truncated-SHA container name, not the full-SHA image tag
findings.finding: The plan assumes the reap point can identify 'the corresponding rebar-mcp-<sha> tag', but the reaped container name embeds the 12-char TRUNCATED SHA (${TARGET:0:12}) while the image is tagged with the FULL $TARGET SHA — the full-SHA image tag is not directly derivable from the truncated container name available at the reap.
findings.location: Scope #1 ('removing the corresponding rebar-mcp-<sha> tag belongs there — after the reap')
scenarios: Retire code tries to `docker rmi $MCP_IMAGE:<name-derived-sha>` but the truncated container SHA does not match the full image tag, so the rmi silently misses and no image is reclaimed

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the retire target from the `rebar-mcp-<sha>` container-name pattern to the actual image tag `compose-mcp:$TARGET`, and specify how the reap loop at autodeploy.sh:460 maps a reaped container back to its image tag.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:146 `MCP_IMAGE="${MCP_IMAGE:-compose-mcp}"`; :763 `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` — images are `compose-mcp:<TARGET>`

autodeploy.sh:147 `MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX="${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX:-rebar-mcp}"`; :783 `mcp_newname="${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}"` — `rebar-mcp-<sha>` is the CONTAINER name, not an image tag
findings.finding: The plan names the retire target as 'its `rebar-mcp-<sha>` image', but `rebar-mcp-<sha>` is the CONTAINER name pattern; MCP images are tagged `compose-mcp:$TARGET` (MCP_IMAGE=compose-mcp). No image bears a `rebar-mcp-<sha>` tag, so the named edit target does not exist as written.
findings.location: Scope item 1 / AC lines 1-2 ('its `rebar-mcp-<sha>` image is removed')
scenarios: Implementer greps for a `rebar-mcp-<sha>` image tag to rmi and finds none
findings.suggested_fix: State the image to remove is `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` (compose-mcp:<full-sha>), and describe deriving `$TARGET` for a reaped container (the container name embeds only `${TARGET:0:12}`, so the mapping is not a direct substring — capture the full SHA at start or via `docker inspect` of the container's image).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Re-express the MCP retire lifeline in terms of the actual MCP tag scheme (`compose-mcp:$TARGET` per SHA + running old container), not the review-bot-only `:prev` tag, and define exactly which `compose-mcp:*` tags AC-1's test asserts survive.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:676 `docker tag "$BOT_IMAGE:latest" "$BOT_IMAGE:prev"` and :689 rollback — `:prev` is applied only to BOT_IMAGE (review-bot)
search for `MCP_IMAGE:prev` returns no matches; no `docker rmi` exists in autodeploy.sh today
findings.finding: The plan tells the MCP retire path to 'Keep the LIVE image and `:prev` as the rollback lifeline', but `:prev` is a BOT_IMAGE-only tag; there is no MCP `:prev` tag in the codebase. The MCP rollback lifeline is the per-SHA `compose-mcp:$TARGET` image plus the still-running old container, not a `:prev` tag.
findings.location: Scope item 1 ('Keep the LIVE image and `:prev` as the rollback lifeline'); AC lines 1-2
scenarios: Test author writes an AC-1 test asserting a `compose-mcp:prev` tag survives, but no such tag is ever created by the MCP flow

findings.checklist_item: Specify the exact image-tag-from-container mapping used at reap: the image is `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` (full sha), the container name carries only `${TARGET:0:12}`, so define how the retire step recovers the full tag (e.g. inspect the exited container's `.Config.Image`, or record the tag at deploy time) and stop describing the tag as `rebar-mcp-<sha>`.
evidence: Plan: 'removing the corresponding `rebar-mcp-<sha>` tag'
autodeploy.sh:763 `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` — image tag is compose-mcp:<full sha>
autodeploy.sh:783 `mcp_newname="${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}"` — container name carries only a 12-char sha + port
autodeploy.sh:460 reap has only the container name `$n`
findings.finding: AC1/AC2 assume the retired image tag is `rebar-mcp-<sha>`, but that is the CONTAINER naming convention; the actual image tag built per deploy is `$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET` (compose-mcp:<full-sha>), and the container name is `${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}` — a TRUNCATED 12-char sha plus a port suffix. At the reap point (autodeploy.sh:460) only the container name is available, from which the full-SHA image tag cannot be reconstructed, so the retire step cannot reliably identify which image to remove.
scenarios: Reap branch fires for an exited container but the code derives the wrong tag string and removes nothing (silent no-op leak persists), or worse computes a tag that doesn't exist
findings.suggested_fix: At reap, read the image reference from the container itself (`docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' "$n"`) and remove THAT tag if it is neither the live image nor `$MCP_IMAGE:prev`, rather than reconstructing a tag string from the container name.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the durable CloudWatch alarm resource (as-code, e.g. in monitoring_autodeploy.tf, actioned to rebar-gerrit-alerts) that pages on the persistent-pressure metric at >=3 consecutive ineffective cycles, so Scope item 3's 'loud, distinct ALARM' is an actual alarm and not merely a published metric.
evidence: Scope: 'Emit a loud, distinct ALARM marker when pressure persists across 3 or more reclaim cycles'
AC5: '...observability.sh publishes it, so it is alarmable without host access.'

Existing pressure signal is backed by a real alarm resource: monitoring_autodeploy.tf aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm 'rebar-root-disk-pressure' — the new persistence signal has no analogous alarm resource specified
findings.finding: Scope item 3 promises a 'loud, distinct ALARM marker' for persistent pressure, and AC5 requires observability.sh to publish the marker so it is 'alarmable without host access' — but neither the Scope nor the ACs require the corresponding CloudWatch alarm resource (an aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm in terraform) that actually pages on the published persistence metric. Publishing a metric makes it alarmABLE but does not create the alarm; the actionable 'reclaim is ineffective' page therefore may not exist as-code.
scenarios: Reclaim runs ineffectively for 3+ cycles; the persistence metric is published but no CloudWatch alarm is wired to rebar-gerrit-alerts, so no page fires and the condition is silent until an incident sweep manually inspects the metric
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC and a terraform aws_cloudwatch_metric_alarm keyed to the new persistence metric (namespace/name published by observability.sh), with alarm_actions/ok_actions = aws_sns_topic.alerts.arn, and confirm it is distinct from rebar-root-disk-pressure (which watches raw df%, not persistence).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the retire target to the actual image scheme (`compose-mcp:$TARGET`), and specify how the reaped container is mapped to its image ref (e.g. `docker inspect -f '{{.Image}}'` captured before `docker rm`), since 'rebar-mcp-<sha>' is the container name (12-char truncated sha) not an image tag.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:147 `MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX="${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX:-rebar-mcp}"` — 'rebar-mcp' names CONTAINERS, not images
autodeploy.sh:783 `mcp_newname="${MCP_CONTAINER_PREFIX}-${TARGET:0:12}-${mcp_newport}"` — container name uses a 12-char TRUNCATED sha and a port suffix
autodeploy.sh:146 `MCP_IMAGE="${MCP_IMAGE:-compose-mcp}"` and autodeploy.sh:763 `docker tag "$MCP_IMAGE" "$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` — the image is `compose-mcp:<full-sha>`

The reaped container's image ref must be derived from the container (e.g. `docker inspect -f '{{.Image}}'`) or mapped to `compose-mcp:$TARGET`; the plan names neither and asserts a nonexistent `rebar-mcp-<sha>` image tag.
findings.finding: The plan's retire-time image removal depends on a 'rebar-mcp-<sha>' IMAGE tag that does not exist: 'rebar-mcp' is the CONTAINER-name prefix and MCP images are tagged 'compose-mcp:<full-sha>'. A removal targeting 'rebar-mcp-<sha>' would no-op and again free nothing while reporting success.
findings.location: Scope item 1 and AC lines 1-2 ('its rebar-mcp-<sha> image is removed'; 'removing the corresponding rebar-mcp-<sha> tag belongs there')
scenarios: Retire path issues `docker rmi rebar-mcp-<sha>` (or image prune keyed on that name) against a box where the only MCP images are `compose-mcp:<full-sha>` — the ref matches nothing and the disk is not reclaimed
A test asserting 'exactly which tags survive' would be written against the wrong tag namespace and pass while production frees nothing
findings.suggested_fix: Before reaping in mcp_retire_sweep, capture the container's image via `img=$(docker inspect -f '{{.Config.Image}}' "$n")` (or resolve `compose-mcp:$TARGET`), then after a successful `docker rm` issue `docker rmi "$img"` guarded to skip the LIVE image and `compose-mcp:latest`/rollback tag; assert against `compose-mcp:*` tags in the test.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Restate the MCP-image retention invariant in terms of the actual scheme: which `compose-mcp:<sha>` tags are kept as the rollback lifeline (e.g. the live backend's sha and the immediately-previous sha), since there is no `compose-mcp:prev` tag for the MCP path.
evidence: autodeploy.sh:676,679,689 show `:prev` is a BOT_IMAGE (review-bot) concept: `docker tag "$BOT_IMAGE:latest" "$BOT_IMAGE:prev"`
The MCP path tags `"$MCP_IMAGE:$TARGET"` per-sha (autodeploy.sh:763) and never creates a `compose-mcp:prev` tag
The comment cited by the plan (autodeploy.sh:272 ':prev is the rollback lifeline') is in prune_docker_caches describing the review-bot invariant, not the MCP retire path the scope edits.
findings.finding: The plan reuses ':prev is the rollback lifeline' language from the review-bot image path, but the MCP blue-green path has no ':prev' tag — it tags per-sha (compose-mcp:$TARGET) and keeps the live backend via the running container / nginx upstream. The AC 'the live image and :prev are retained' names a retention target that does not exist for MCP images.
findings.location: Scope item 1 and AC lines 1 ('Keep the LIVE image and :prev as the rollback lifeline')
scenarios: An implementer or test asserts survival of a `compose-mcp:prev` tag that is never created, or removes the previous-sha image the operator intended as the MCP rollback lifeline

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Extend AC3's proving check to also assert the delta value appears in the log line (and matches after-minus-before), not just before and after.
evidence: 'logs root-disk free space BEFORE and AFTER, and the delta, on every invocation (checked by asserting both values appear in the emitted log line)'
The verify clause names two values while the criterion text names three (before, after, delta)
findings.finding: AC3 requires logging free space BEFORE, AFTER, and 'the delta', but the proving check only asserts 'both values appear' — it does not assert the delta is present or computed correctly.
scenarios: Implementer logs before/after but omits or miscomputes the delta; the stated test still passes
findings.suggested_fix: Change the verify clause to: 'checked by asserting all three (before, after, delta) appear and delta == after - before'.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how a failed `docker rmi rebar-mcp-<sha>` is surfaced (logged/non-swallowed) rather than silently treated as success, so a stuck retire is observable.
evidence: Scope: 'removing the corresponding rebar-mcp-<sha> tag belongs there — after the reap'
No mention of error handling if `docker rmi` returns non-zero
A swallowed rmi failure would silently defeat the entire fix (disk keeps filling) yet report success — the exact failure mode this plan exists to eliminate
findings.finding: The retire path performs a destructive `docker rmi` of the rebar-mcp-<sha> tag but the plan does not state what happens if that removal fails (e.g. the image is still referenced by another tag or a lingering container).
scenarios: docker rmi of a <sha> tag fails because the image is still in use; retire logs success but frees nothing
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC: the retire path logs a distinct warning (and does not report retirement success) when `docker rmi` of the <sha> tag returns non-zero, so an un-retirable image is visible in logs.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State whether the 3-cycle persistence threshold is a named/configurable constant (like BUILD_CACHE_KEEP) rather than an inline literal.
evidence: 'At 3 or more consecutive ineffective cycles, a distinct marker is emitted'
Neighboring values BUILD_CACHE_KEEP (5GB) and PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL (600s) are named constants
A persistence threshold likely to be tuned after operational experience is a changeability candidate
findings.finding: The '3 or more consecutive ineffective cycles' persistence threshold is hardcoded as a literal in the acceptance criteria, with no indication it is configurable, despite living beside existing tunables like BUILD_CACHE_KEEP and PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL.
scenarios: Operators later want the ineffective-cycle alarm to fire after 2 or 5 cycles and must edit code instead of config
findings.suggested_fix: Introduce a named constant (e.g. PRESSURE_INEFFECTIVE_CYCLES=3) alongside the existing tunables and reference it in AC5.

findings.checklist_item: Define the persistent-pressure counter's persistence (a STATE_DIR file, like PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE) and state whether a 'cycle' is a throttled reclaim attempt vs a no-op tick, so 'consecutive ineffective cycles' is unambiguous and survives the per-tick process boundary.
evidence: Plan: 'a persistent-pressure counter increments; it resets to zero once the disk falls below the threshold'
autodeploy.sh:307 reclaim is gated by PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL=600s — reclaims are ~10min apart and skipped in between
ABSENCE: no state-file named (contrast PRESSURE_PRUNE_TS_FILE at :133 which the existing throttle persists across ticks)
findings.finding: AC4-6 require a persistent-pressure COUNTER that survives across cycles and increments only on consecutive ineffective reclaims, but the plan does not name a persistence mechanism (each autodeploy tick is a fresh process) nor define what a 'cycle' is relative to the existing 600s reclaim throttle (PRESSURE_PRUNE_MIN_INTERVAL). Without pinning both, '3 or more consecutive ineffective cycles' is ambiguous and the counter could reset every tick.
findings.location: Scope item 3 / AC lines 4-5; autodeploy.sh:299-316 (reclaim_under_pressure, throttled)
scenarios: Counter kept in a shell variable resets to 0 every tick and never reaches 3; or a 'cycle' is counted per no-op tick rather than per actual reclaim, so the >=3 threshold fires on unrelated timing
